subject: History

internalBreakdown.component: Project: planning, organisation and data collection (August-October)

textbooks: Themes in World History, Class XI (NCERT)
notes: Each theme opens with a timeline introduction: Timeline I (6 MYA to 1 BCE), II (c. 100 BCE to 1300 CE), III (c. 1300 to 1700), IV (c. 1700 to 2000).
Theme topics are summarised from the document's learning-outcome column, which is the only content column it gives for most themes.
Maps from official Government of India websites may be used.

chapters.name: Writing and City Life
topics: Focus: Iraq, 3rd millennium BCE
Growth of towns
Nature of early urban societies
Historians' debate on uses of writing
outcomes: Elucidate the social and cultural aspects of civilisation to connect city life with the culture of contemporary civilisations through their writings
Analyse the outcomes of a sustained tradition of writing
Explain the connection between the growth of civilisation and the tradition of writing

chapters.name: An Empire Across Three Continents
topics: The Roman Empire: polity, economy, society and culture
Roman contacts with the subcontinent's empires
Slavery
Cultural transformation
outcomes: Explain the dynamics of the Roman Empire to understand its polity, economy, society and culture
Analyse the implications of Roman contacts with the subcontinent and discuss slavery
Examine the cultural transformation of the period and the impact of slavery

chapters.name: Nomadic Empires
topics: Living patterns of nomadic pastoralist society
Rise of Genghis Khan
Socio-political and economic change under his descendants
Mongol and world perspectives on Genghis Khan
outcomes: Identify the living patterns of nomadic pastoralist society
Trace the rise and growth of Genghis Khan
Analyse socio-political and economic changes under the descendants of Genghis Khan
Distinguish between the Mongol perspective and the world's opinion of Genghis Khan

chapters.name: The Three Orders
topics: Feudalism: first, second, third and fourth orders of society
Ancient slavery and serfdom
The fourteenth century crisis and the rise of nation states
outcomes: Explain aspects of feudalism with reference to the orders of society
Relate ancient slavery and serfdom
Assess the fourteenth century crisis and the rise of nation states

chapters.name: Changing Cultural Traditions
topics: Renaissance, humanism and realism in the Italian cities
Women in the Renaissance period
Architecture, art and literature
Reformation and the Catholic Church's response
Scientific Revolution and Age of Exploration
outcomes: Analyse the causes, events and effects of the Renaissance, Reformation, Scientific Revolution and Age of Exploration
Relate the facets of Italian cities to the characteristics of Renaissance, humanism and realism
Compare the condition of women in the Renaissance period
Recognise major influences on architectural, artistic and literary developments
Evaluate the Roman Catholic Church's response to the Protestant Reformation

chapters.name: Displacing Indigenous Peoples
topics: Displacement of native peoples in America and Australia
European settlement in Australia and America
Lives and roles of indigenous peoples
outcomes: Evaluate the displacement of native peoples in the development of America and Australia
Analyse European settlement in Australia and America
Compare the lives and roles of indigenous peoples in these continents

chapters.name: Paths to Modernisation
topics: Japan: from imperialism to modernisation; nationalism before and after the Second World War
China: nationalist upsurge from Sun Yat-sen to Mao Zedong
China's path to modernisation under Deng Xiaoping and Zhou Enlai
Korea
outcomes: Summarise the nationalist upsurge in China from Sun Yat-sen to Mao Zedong
Analyse China's path to modernisation under Deng Xiaoping and Zhou Enlai
Deduce the histories of China and Japan from imperialism to modernisation
Analyse Japanese nationalism before and after the Second World War
notes: All three (Japan, China and Korea) must be taught.

chapters.name: Map Work (World History)
topics: Map work of the related themes
